species.name: Red-eared slider
species.summary: An introduced freshwater turtle established after unwanted pets were released.
species.identification: Olive-brown domed shell with yellow streaks and a broad red patch behind each eye. Adults commonly have shells around 15–20 cm long.

species.behaviour: Moves between water and basking sites. It may slide quickly into water when approached.

species.ecologicalRole: An introduced omnivore that can compete with native freshwater wildlife for food and basking sites.
species.pressures: Habitat considerations: Pet release spreads this species into new wetlands. Releasing or abandoning animals in parks is illegal.
species.singapore: NParks describes it as an exotic species found in many Singapore ponds and reservoirs after pet releases.

after.name: Eurasian tree sparrow

after.identification: Chestnut crown, white cheeks with a black cheek spot, black throat patch and brown streaked wings. Both sexes look alike.

after.ecologicalRole: Eats seeds and invertebrates and provides prey for urban predators.
after.pressures: Habitat considerations: Sealed building cavities and loss of seed-rich open ground can reduce nesting and feeding spaces.

after.name: Oriental whip snake
after.summary: A slender tree snake whose green body blends into leaves and thin branches.
after.identification: Long, narrow body, pointed snout, yellow eyes and horizontal pupils. Adults are often bright green; juveniles can be brown.
after.diet: Mainly lizards, plus frogs and small birds.

after.behaviour: Moves through foliage and relies on camouflage. When threatened, it may hold out its tongue as a warning.
after.reproduction: Retains eggs inside the body until they hatch, then gives birth to live young.
after.ecologicalRole: A small predator of lizards, frogs and birds in tree and shrub food webs.
after.pressures: Habitat considerations: Clearing connected shrubs and mangroves removes hunting cover. Persecution caused by fear can kill harmlessly resting snakes.

after.name: Red-eared slider
after.summary: An introduced freshwater turtle established after unwanted pets were released.
after.identification: Olive-brown domed shell with yellow streaks and a broad red patch behind each eye. Adults commonly have shells around 15–20 cm long.

after.activity: Feeds by day and often basks on rocks, logs and banks.

after.reproduction: Lays shelled eggs in nests dug on land; hatchlings move towards freshwater.
after.ecologicalRole: An introduced omnivore that can compete with native freshwater wildlife for food and basking sites.
after.pressures: Habitat considerations: Pet release spreads this species into new wetlands. Releasing or abandoning animals in parks is illegal.
after.singapore: NParks describes it as an exotic species found in many Singapore ponds and reservoirs after pet releases.
